text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said he was not optimistic of a coalition government between the National Front and Malaysian Islamic Party in Kelantan state, but added that he was willing to discuss the matter further. Mahathir was commenting on a statement by Kelantan chief minister Nik Abdul Aziz that his party was willing to form a coalition state government with Mahathir's United Malays National Organisation.

-- Malaysian car maker Proton and British sports car maker Group Lotus will work with U.K.-based University of East Anglia to produce Malaysian engineering graduates with hands-on experience, Mahathir said.

-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad revealed that Proton's deposit for its 206 million ringgit stake in Group Lotus was paid in cash because a British bank refused to accept Proton's cheque. He said the bank refused to accept the cheque because it wanted to block the purchase.
-- Mahathir said Malaysia and other developing nations should reject the move by the European Union (EU) to impose the multilateral investment agreement on them.
